echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'

content.text:
{
  "key": "pr-1343",
  "fields": {
    "summary": "gh-1332 [fix] Finding-identity registry: deduplicate review findings across rounds (hash identity, propose/confirm matching, provenance states)",
    "description": "Closes #1332
# gh-1332 — Cross-round review-thread dedup (finding-identity registry)

## What was built

A persistent, machine-authored **finding-identity registry** that makes every
review thread a first-class citizen with a stable ID, so the next review round
inherits the earlier rounds' verdicts instead of re-raising duplicates.

- `js/common/findingRegistry.js` — round-scoped findings F1–Fn: fingerprinting
  (`{claim, file, line}` with smart line normalization), metadata identity
  matching (same file → same defect; different file → new), unambiguous
  `MERGE F2 INTO F1` resolution, **candidates pending confirmation**
  (reviewer confirms `same`/`new` per candidate), `"fixed"`, `"withdrawn"`
  (reason required) and `"re-introduced"` dispositions, and the per-round
  new-identity convergence census for escalation packets.
- The registry rides on ONE durable machine-authored PR comment per round
  (marker `<!-- dmtools:finding-registry round:N -->`, identity SHA-256 of the
  canonical payload, verify-and-fail-closed parse).
- Reviewer instructions: `instructions/pr_review/general_guidelines.md` §9 —
  answer the registry before raising anything new (verify fixed with citable
  hunks, withdraw with reasons, mark re-introduced; dedup can only escalate).

## Wiring (additive everywhere, never a behavior change without the marker)

- `js/postPRReviewComments.js` — posting time: stamp the round's registry
  comment, add the `review_round_N` label (mirrors `rework-round-N`), apply
  the reviewer's dispositions/confirmations from
  `pr_review.json.findingReview`, echo dedup outcomes. Non-fatal end to end.
- `js/preparePRForReview.js` — context prep: inject
  `input/TICKET/pr_findings.md` (previously raised findings) from the PR's
  latest trusted registry.
- `js/smAgent.js` — loop-guard escalation packets append the finding-identity
  census: per-round new-identity series + BLOCKING withdrawal reasons.

## Identity policy (fail-closed, convention-wide)

Machine identity comes from config (`machineAuthor`, default `ai-teammate`),
resolvable also from the git author allowlist — **an empty allowlist trusts
nothing**: config wins over actors, no false positives, no false negatives.

## Tests

`js/common/findingRegistry.js` + `js/unit-tests/test_findingRegistry.js`
(65 tests: fingerprinting, smart line normalization, metadata matching, MERGE
resolution, candidates, dispositions, census, canonical rendering, comment
lifecycle) + wiring suites extended (`postPReviewComments`,
`preparePRForReview`, `smAgent`) + downstream require-map fixes.
Full suite: **7949 passed, 0 failed**. Snapshots/docs regenerated."
  }
}

arguments.content:
🚨 **BLOCKING: `-->` in `withdrawReason`/`fixHunk` corrupts the registry marker — state silently reverts and payload text leaks onto the PR**

The marker protocol embeds the registry payload as JSON inside an HTML comment (`<!-- dmtools:finding-registry {json} -->`). Claims are safe — `normalizeClaim` strips punctuation — but `applyDisposition` stores `disposition.reason` and `disposition.hunk` **raw** (`item.withdrawReason = String(disposition.reason).trim()`), and `buildRegistryComment` serializes them verbatim into the payload. Neither HTML comments nor `extractMarkerJson`'s suffix search can tolerate a `-->` sequence:

1. **On GitHub**, the comment visually terminates at the injected `-->`; the JSON tail leaks into the visible PR thread as garbage text.
2. **On the next round**, `reviewVerdicts.extractMarkerJson` cuts the payload at the **first** ` -->`, `JSON.parse` fails, `registryFromPayload` returns null, the record is skipped — and `latestRegistry` silently falls back to the **previous** round's registry. The reviewer's withdrawal (and everything else registered in the corrupting round) is lost, so the finding stays open and must be re-answered.

Verified repro against this branch (mermaid arrows are pervasive in this repo's comment style, so a reason like `"not a defect: A --> B is handled upstream"` is a realistic trigger):

```
round 2: withdraw F1 with reason "not a defect: A --> B is handled upstream"
buildRegistryComment(...) → "<!-- dmtools:finding-registry {...,\"withdrawReason\":\"not a defect: A --> B is handled upstream\"...} -->"
latestRegistry([that comment], allow) → null          ← round-2 registry unparseable
extractMarkerJson → null (JSON.parse failed)          ← falls back to round 1
```

Suggested fix — sanitize at the boundary where strings enter the payload (either in `applyDisposition` or in `buildRegistryComment` before `JSON.stringify`), e.g. strip or replace marker-hostile sequences from every embedded string field (`withdrawReason`, `fixHunk`, and any future free-text):

```js
function markerSafe(text) {
    return String(text || '').replace(/-->/g, '--\u200b>').replace(/<!--/g, '\u200b');
}
```

(and assert the built body contains exactly one marker suffix, or reject/strip on serialization). The escalation-comment renderer (`buildEscalationPacketComment`) echoes raw reasons too — same treatment there keeps the visible census well-formed.

The unit suite has no round-trip test for marker-hostile payload content — worth adding alongside the fix (`withdrawReason` containing `-->` must still parse back, with the sanitized text preserved for display).

💡 **SUGGESTION: comment-list normalization duplicated across the two wiring sites**

`prCommentsForRegistry` (postPRReviewComments.js:1093) and `prCommentListForRegistry` (preparePRForReview.js:243) implement the same "raw comments → array" ladder (`typeof raw === 'string' ? JSON.parse : raw`, then `Array.isArray(obj) ? obj : (obj.comments || obj.items || [])`) with only the error policy differing (catch-and-null vs let-the-caller's-catch-handle). Two independent copies of a parse ladder are exactly the kind of thing that drifts — e.g. if the payload gains another envelope shape, one site gets fixed and the other silently keeps returning `[]`.

Consider hoisting one helper (e.g. `normalizePrCommentList(raw)` in `findingRegistry.js`, or a shared `js/common/` leaf both files already require) and keeping the try/catch policy at each call site. All verification checks pass. The review is complete.

## Review Summary — PR #1343 (gh-1332: finding-identity registry)

**Verdict: `REQUEST_CHANGES`** — 2 BLOCKING, 0 IMPORTANT, 3 SUGGESTION.

**🚨 BLOCKING 1 — Red CI.** The `crap` check failed on head `06e63285`: `CRAP ratchet failed: CRAP may only decrease` — 12 new functions over threshold (worst: `findingRegistry.js::applyRound` CC 33, CRAP 33; `matchFinding` 16.1; `prCommentsForRegistry`/`stampFindingRegistry`/`postFindingRegistryUpdate` in the wiring). The unit suite itself is green (7966 passed / 0 failed in CI; the single local failure I hit, `sessionDelta`, is pre-existing and environment-dependent, untouched by this PR). Fix is a pure refactor per the repo's own gh-1195 split pattern.

**🚨 BLOCKING 2 — Marker payload corruption (verified with a runnable repro against this branch).** Claims are normalized (punctuation stripped), but `withdrawReason`/`fixHunk` are stored **raw** and serialized into the `<!-- dmtools:finding-registry {json} -->` HTML-comment marker. A `-->` in a reviewer-supplied reason (e.g. a quoted mermaid arrow — pervasive in this repo) terminates the HTML comment early: on GitHub the JSON tail leaks as visible text, and on the next round `extractMarkerJson` cuts at the first `-->`, `JSON.parse` fails, and `latestRegistry` **silently falls back to the previous round** — the reviewer's disposition is lost. My repro printed exactly that: round-2 registry unparseable, dedup state reverted. Fix: sanitize marker-hostile sequences at the payload boundary + add a round-trip test for marker-hostile content.

**What's good:** the core design is genuinely solid — propose/confirm two-stage matching with a confirm-only merge bias, escalate-only severity merges, fail-closed machine-author gate (empty allowlist trusts nothing, verified), resolved identities leaving the dedup space, additive wiring into all three call sites with thorough behavior-driven tests (57 in the new suite), GralJS-clean code, hoisted requires per gh-823.

**💡 Suggestions:** duplicated comment-list normalization across the two wiring files; unused `repoInfo` param in `postFindingRegistryUpdate`; dead duplicate `'./common/findingRegistry.js'` keys in two test require maps. Also noted in the general comment: stale PR-description metrics (57 tests, not 65; CI ran 7966, not 7949) and "SHA-256" actually implemented as double FNV-1a.

Artifacts written: `outputs/pr_review.json`, `outputs/pr_review_general.md` (15 lines), `outputs/pr_review_comments/comment{1-5}.md` — all 5 inline anchors verified as added lines in the PR diff at the stated line numbers; no `response.md` (review-only flow). CodeGraph was unavailable; grep fallback was used and documented for impact analysis (require maps, `reviewPolicy` consumers, `machineAuthor` glue, `scm.getPrComments` shapes, secret-pattern sweep — clean).
